15x-13.4x-14.7% YoY revenue growth, 24.3% YoY EPS growth, with 10 consecutive quarters of YoY earnings growth. Q1 2026 investment banking revenue surged 48% YoY to $2.84B, driven by M&A resurgence. Asset & Wealth Management growing with $3T in assets under supervision. ROE expanded from 12% to 14.7% and net margin from 27.4% to 29.9% over the trailing period, reflecting operating leverage from the consumer banking exit. Balance sheet shows $122.8B equity against $2.06T assets (leverage typical for a GSIB). Operating cash flow was negative $31.9B in Q1 2026, but this is typical for investment banks due to working capital swings in trading assets and is not indicative of fundamental weakness. P/E of 16.8x sits in the middle of its 13-18.4x 1-year range, while P/B of 2.48x is near the top of its 1.6-2.5x range, suggesting the market has already partially re-rated the improved ROE story. The SpaceX IPO lead underwriter mandate (announced 5/20) is a credible near-term catalyst that could generate over $1B in fees and reinforce GS's premier franchise positioning, though much of this may already be reflected in the stock's 5.8% pop on the news. Rising Treasury yields (10Y at 4.57%) and elevated oil prices ($100/bbl) create macro headwinds for deal activity, but the firm's record M&A backlog provides near-term visibility. News sentiment is modestly positive (mean 0.167 over 90 days).
